collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Teens organize a gathering to protect the shrinking reef: march to the elders, or start fixing it themselves.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) have counted the fish on the reef every week for a year, and the count keeps falling. They want the village to do something. The elders keep saying they will discuss it. What should the teens do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The teens gather outside the elders' hut with their counting sticks and refuse to leave until they are heard. The elders are startled, then impressed by the counts. The reef is rested for a season.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The teens start replanting broken coral and pulling out the weed that is choking it. It is slow. The elders notice, and quietly join in. Nobody ever has a meeting about it.
